rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Output Used by a Downstream Component ('Injection')
rules.description: Using user-controlled data to create a template can lead to remote code execution or cross site scripting.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
rules.description: Passing user supplied arguments to a Javascript to Python translation engine such as Js2Py can lead to remote code execution.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
rules.description: Extracting files from a malicious ZIP file, or similar type of archive, without validating that the destination file path is within the destination directory can allow an attacker to unexpectedly gain access to resources.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code ('Eval Injection')
rules.description: Interpreting unsanitized user input as code allows a malicious user to perform arbitrary code execution.

rules.cwe_name: Dead Code
rules.description: A statement has no effect

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Data within XPath Expressions ('XPath Injection')
rules.description: Building a XPath query from user-controlled sources is vulnerable to insertion of malicious Xpath code by the user.

rules.cwe_name: Use of Obsolete Function
rules.description: Import of a deprecated module

rules.cwe_name: Improper Link Resolution Before File Access ('Link Following')
rules.description: File access follows a symlink, hardlink, or shortcut to an unintended resource.

rules.cwe_name: Function Call With Incorrect Number of Arguments
rules.description: A string formatting operation, such as '"%s: %s, %s" % (a,b)', where the number of conversion specifiers in the format string differs from the number of values to be formatted will raise a TypeError.

rules.cwe_name: Observable Timing Discrepancy
rules.description: When checking a Hash over a message, a constant-time algorithm should be used. Otherwise, an attacker may be able to forge a valid Hash for an arbitrary message by running a timing attack if they can send to the validation procedure. A successful attack can result in authentication bypass.
